This step runs before any model is fitted so that structural problems are known before the interaction test is interpreted.
steps.question: Do the 16 brain RNA-seq samples group by genotype (WT, KO), by treatment (vehicle, drug), or by neither, and is any of the four cells driven by an outlier or by library depth?

grounding.reason: Raw counts before a model: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap per R-0033@40bf.

constraints: Use the variance stabilizing transformation with blind=TRUE (blind to the design)
PCA on the 500 most variable genes
Colour every plot by genotype, by treatment, and by the 4-level condition
Do not filter, drop, or impute samples in this step — flag only
steps.description: Load counts.csv (12,000 genes x 16 samples, gene symbol in the first column) and metadata.csv, verify that sample identifiers match exactly and that the design is the stated balanced 2x2 with 4 samples per genotype-treatment cell. Apply the DESeq2 variance stabilizing transformation blind to the design, compute a PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and draw a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap. steps.name: DESeq2 interaction model and Wald test
caveats: The interaction test is underpowered at n=4 per cell: a short or empty significant list is the expected outcome of a modest true differential response, not evidence that the drug acts identically in both genotypes. State this in the output.
The interaction coefficient says the effects differ; it does not say the drug has any effect in either genotype. That requires the simple effects from T1S3.
steps.context: The interaction coefficient genotypeKO.treatmentdrug is the direct statistical answer to 'does the drug act differently in knockout than in wild type'. With 4 replicates per cell it is a difference of differences with a standard error roughly twice that of a simple effect, so power is low by construction. DESeq2 1.52.0 and ashr 2.2-63 are present in the environment.
steps.question: Which genes show a drug effect (drug vs vehicle) that differs in magnitude between KO and WT — i.e. which genes have a non-zero genotypeKO:treatmentdrug interaction coefficient?

grounding.reason: 2x2 interaction question on raw counts with 4 replicates per cell: DESeq2 with an interaction term and a Wald test on the interaction coefficient (R-0013), ashr shrinkage because downstream contrasts are not single coefficients (R-0040), BH with independent filtering at alpha 0.05 (R-0010). tximport (R-0018) is not applicable — the input is an already-summarized gene-level count matrix, not salmon quant files, so no length offsets are available.

constraints: Set reference levels with an explicit relevel/factor call: genotype ref WT, treatment ref vehicle — never rely on alphabetical order
Feed raw integer counts to DESeq2; do not CPM-, TPM-, or log-transform before the model
Pre-filter minimally (>=10 counts in >=4 samples) and leave independent filtering enabled to do the rest
Pass alpha=0.05 to results() so the independent filter is optimized for the reporting cutoff
Keep the DESeq2 Cook's-distance outlier behaviour on (with n=4 per cell it flags and sets p to NA rather than replacing counts) and report the flagged genes separately from filter-driven NAs
Shrink with ashr, not apeglm — later steps need shrinkage for contrasts that are not a single coefficient, and the same estimator must be used throughout

steps.name: Preranked GSEA per contrast

Long and highly expressed genes are easier to call in count data; the tested-genes universe removes part of that bias but not all of it

Reference store holds MSigDB human hallmark 2026.1, MSigDB human GO (BP/CC/MF) 2026.1, and WikiPathways human 2026.07.10.
steps.question: Which biological processes show a coordinated differential drug response between KO and WT, and which respond to drug within each genotype separately?

grounding.reason: Ranked fgsea on the full tested list is the default enrichment (R-0107); human data takes hallmark first then further collections from the store (R-0048, R-0165); the disputed ranking metric (R-0108) is settled here in favour of the Wald statistic and stated. Run enrichment once per contrast; never pool genes from several contrasts into one list
Use human gene set collections only — the data is Homo sapiens, taxon 9606
Set and record a random seed before the permutation test
Apply the same size window and the same universe (the tested genes) to every collection
Do not run an over-representation test on the significant gene lists if they hold fewer than ~50 genes; report the list size and rely on the ranked test

Map the gene symbols in the ranked list to the identifier space of the gene set collections and report the share of tested genes that did not map and the share with a many-to-many mapping. Collection name and release version reported for each collection used; random seed recorded

steps.context: This is the deliverable that answers the research question. The interaction coefficient is the answer, but it is only interpretable beside the two simple effects and beside an honest statement of power.
steps.question: Taken together, does the drug act differently in KO than in WT, and with what confidence given 4 replicates per cell?

grounding.reason: R-0092 requires the two simple effects and the interaction contrast side by side with the reference levels named; R-0085 and R-0087 fix the effect columns and the two fit diagnostics; R-0041, R-0051, R-0086 fix the reporting and reproducibility fields.

constraints: Report the simple effect in WT, the simple effect in KO, and the interaction contrast side by side — never the interaction coefficient alone
Name the reference level of each factor beside every table
Rank and plot on the shrunken log2 fold change; never rank on the unshrunken estimate alone
State the enrichment method-dependence caveat explicitly
Do not present any gene or gene set as an established finding — they are hypotheses at this sample size
steps.description: Assemble the reporting artifact. Build a per-gene table placing the three quantities side by side: drug effect in WT, drug effect in KO, and the interaction contrast, each with unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, and ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange, plus padj per contrast. Genes ranked and plotted by the shrunken log2 fold change; p-values taken from the unshrunken fit
Volcano plot for the interaction contrast and per-cell expression panels for the top interaction genes

Report states: design formula, reference levels WT and vehicle with the meaning of each coefficient, filter threshold, genes tested, FDR cutoff and its per-contrast scope, DE counts per contrast, NA counts split into outlier-flagged versus filter-removed

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness check
caveats: Method disagreement is expected at 4 replicates per cell and is itself informative — a gene called by one method only is a weaker candidate, not a contradiction
This step is a robustness check, not an independent confirmation: both methods use the same 16 samples

steps.question: Does a second method on the same counts and the same interaction design agree on which genes show a differential drug response between KO and WT?

grounding.reason: R-0001 names the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the second method at 2-11 replicates per group, and R-0042 fixes the reporting as per-method counts plus the intersection as the high-confidence set.

constraints: Use the same filtered count matrix and the same design and reference levels as T1S2 so the comparison is method-only
Use TMM scaling factors inside the edgeR model; do not feed pre-normalized values
Use the quasi-likelihood F-test (glmQLFTest), not the classic exact test — the design has an interaction term
Report the overlap; do not merge the two gene lists into a union
steps.description: Fit the same design (~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, WT and vehicle as references) on the same filtered count matrix with edgeR: TMM normalization factors, estimateDisp, glmQLFit, and glmQLFTest on the interaction coefficient. Report the number of genes significant at BH-adjusted p < 0.05 from edgeR, the number from the DESeq2 Wald test in T1S2, and the size of their intersection. acceptance_criteria: edgeR QL fit uses the identical design formula, identical reference levels, and the identical filtered gene set as T1S2
TMM normalization factors used (not DESeq2 size factors, and no pre-scaled counts)
Three numbers reported: DESeq2 significant interaction genes, edgeR significant interaction genes, size of the intersection
The intersection is labelled the high-confidence set; method-specific calls are listed separately with the calling method named
The union is not presented as the result

plan.title: KO x drug interaction DE in human brain RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question — does the drug act differently in knockout than in wild type — is a genotype x treatment interaction question on a balanced 2x2 factorial design: genotype (WT, KO) x treatment (vehicle, drug), 4 biological replicates per cell, 16 samples, 12,000 genes of raw salmon-derived integer counts in counts.csv with the sample table in metadata.csv (16 rows: genotype, treatment, condition). No batch variable is recorded, so the design carries no nuisance term; if the metadata holds a hidden processing structure it would show as a PCA axis in T1S1 and must be reported rather than silently modelled.

The plan is a single DESeq2 track plus an enrichment track. T1S1 does sample structure QC on the blind VST (PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes), coloured by genotype, treatment and their 4-level combination, before any model is fitted — this is where an outlier cell or an unbalanced depth would be caught. T1S2 fits ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment with WT and vehicle set explicitly as reference levels and tests the genotypeKO.treatmentdrug interaction coefficient with the Wald test; this coefficient is the literal answer to the question. T1S3 extracts the two simple effects — drug vs vehicle within WT (the main treatment coefficient) and drug vs vehicle within KO (main + interaction) — as named contrasts, so that the interaction is read beside the effects it is a difference of. Log fold changes are shrunk with ashr (not apeglm) because the KO simple effect is a sum of coefficients rather than a single coefficient; p-values come from the unshrunken fit. BH adjustment with independent filtering is applied within each contrast at alpha 0.05, and the p-value histogram is inspected before the adjustment is trusted.

Power is the central caveat and the plan states it up front. An interaction coefficient is a difference of differences: its standard error is roughly twice that of a simple effect, and with 4 replicates per cell the test has low power. A small or empty interaction gene list is therefore the expected outcome under a real but modest differential drug response, and it is not evidence that the drug acts the same way in both genotypes. For that reason the enrichment step (T2S1) runs preranked fgsea on the full ranked list of tested genes using the DESeq2 Wald statistic as the ranking metric — a coordinated shift across a pathway can be detectable when no individual gene clears FDR. The disputed ranking-metric choice is settled here in favour of the Wald statistic: it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, which matters most precisely where the per-gene evidence is weak. Enrichment is run separately per contrast (interaction, WT simple effect, KO simple effect) and never on a pooled list, and against MSigDB Hallmark human first, then GO BP and human WikiPathways as follow-up collections, each with its release stated. T1S4 assembles the report: the three results side by side per gene, MA and dispersion diagnostics, counts of genes with NA p-values split by cause (Cook's outlier flag versus independent filter — with 4 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags rather than replaces outliers), and the reproducibility record.

T1S5 is a robustness check rather than a new result: the same design and counts fitted with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test, reporting the number of significant interaction genes from each method and the size of the intersection, with the intersection as the high-confidence set. It is separated from the main track so that a failure there does not cost the primary analysis.
